videos.script: Lesson one sent JSON to an address, and the address named a thing. {{rest}} This lesson asks something else. What if a program could call a function that lives on another machine? {{call}} That is a remote procedure call. gRPC is the version most companies run between their own services today. {{grpc}} You write the contract first, in a proto file. A compiler turns it into code for the client and for the server. {{proto}} Then you look at what really travels. Thirty-three bytes, where the same book in JSON took eighty-five. {{bytes}} You build a stock service for the bookshop's warehouse. It answers a question, streams the changes as they happen, and takes a delivery box by box. And it fails the way a remote call fails, with a status and a deadline. {{stream}} Last, you see where it stops fitting. A browser cannot call it directly, and a public API rarely should. {{choose}}
